title: Heliox Dataworks Dedicated Capacity Intake
summary: Initial discovery on dedicated GPU reservations, tenant isolation, burst/overprovisioning strategy, and scaling expectations for Heliox's real-time genomic inference product. Discussed hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs, VPC/connectivity, KMS, and benchmark plan. Agreed to run a two-week proof benchmark on a small reserved pool and follow up with pricing and an architecture workshop.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-29 14:30 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Priya (CTO, Heliox), Evan (Infra Lead), Li (ML Eng)

Summary (auto): Discussed dedicated capacity sizing, isolation options (node-level vs pool-level vs tenant microseg), burst model, pre-warm pools, and security controls. Action: Redwood to send pricing + benchmark plan.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros — i'm maya, i'm the AE on this account, carlos is our se, go ahead priya?
[00:18] Priya (Heliox): yeah hi, i'm priya, cto at heliox, we build a realtime genomic insights service — latency sensitive, and we have a hard SLA for our clinical partners, so isolation and data residency are big for us.
[00:34] Evan (Heliox): evan here, infra lead; main asks: predictable throughput, no noisy neighbor surprises, and a clear plan for bursts during nightly pipelines.
[00:46] Carlos (Redwood): great, thanks. quick framing: we'll cover dedicated reserved pools, isolation options, burst/burstback strategies, and what a pilot looks like. feel free to interrupt.
[00:58] Priya: sounds good. first-level question — why would we pick dedicated over hosted? we're worried about cost but also about p95 and data control.
[01:12] Maya: good. hosted is fastest to production but for strict isolation and committed throughput dedicated gives you reserved gpus and tenancy guarantees, plus VPC peering / private endpoints. cost-wise reserved pools give a better unit price once you commit.
[01:28] Priya: okay, and private (on-prem) is an option if we need full air-gap later?
[01:34] Carlos: yes — private deployments are available but involve separate packaging. for now dedicated in a customer-segregated cluster with KMS integration usually hits the balance.
[01:46] Li (Heliox): our model is large — 16k context, kv-cache heavy. how does the runtime handle long contexts and batching? any quantization constraints?
[02:00] Carlos: runtime uses continuous batching and kv-cache management; for long context workloads we tune the kernel selection — we also support int8 and some mixed-quant flows, but model accuracy checks are needed. sometimes quantization hurts edge-case outputs so you can pin models without quantization in the pool.
[02:22] Evan: for isolation, we're thinking per-tenant node pinning vs logical isolation within a shared pool — pros/cons?
[02:30] Carlos: node pinning gives strongest isolation but less efficient utilization. shared pools with strict cgroup/tenant limits plus warm pools is more cost efficient. we often recommend a hybrid: customer-critical tenants on pinned nodes, background low-priority on shared.
[02:52] Priya: that hybrid sounds promising. what about burst: we have spiky loads during dataset ingest windows, can we burst beyond reserved capacity?
[03:05] Maya: yes — dedicated supports burst to a higher capacity tier when available. we can define burst policies: max burst % over baseline, prewarm thresholds, and auto-fallback to hosted models if dedicated is saturated.
[03:19] Evan: fallback to hosted — any data residency flags there? we can't send PHI to hosted tiers, so fallback can't be to hosted in our case.
[03:28] Carlos: understood — in that scenario we'd recommend a cold standby reserved pool in another region or a hot spare warm pool — both reserved — to maintain residency and compliance.
[03:40] Li: how fast does pre-warm happen? if we spin up a warm pool at peak it feels like cold start delays could kill our p95.
[03:50] Carlos: warm pools keep model shards and kv-cache resident; pre-warm to full readiness takes on the order of seconds to low tens of seconds depending on model size. we add prewarming heuristics based on recent traffic.
[04:08] Priya: okay. what's the quant for "seconds"? our p95 target is 350ms for 8k sequences in production.
[04:20] Carlos: 350ms p95 for 8k is tight but reachable with dedicated pinned nodes and tuned batching; the main gains are avoiding network hops and keeping kv-cache hot. we should run a focused benchmark.
[04:34] Maya: agreed. we'll propose a benchmark that mirrors your 8k sequence profile.
[04:40] Evan: security check — we need SOC2, KMS with customer-managed keys, SAML SSO, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. any of that an issue?
[04:52] Carlos: we support SOC2-compliant hosting, KMS integrations (bring-your-own-key), SAML SSO and RBAC, and audit logs with configurable retention and SIEM forwarding. small caveat: for on-prem private installs, some of the telemetry hooks are opt-in.
[05:10] Priya: good. do you support HSM-backed keys?
[05:14] Maya: yes, we have KMS/HSM options in enterprise tiers.
[05:20] Priya: what about tenant-level audit trails? we need per-request traceability tied to tokens.
[05:26] Carlos: token-level tracing and per-route cost/latency breakdowns are in the console, and we can emit traces to your tracing system. there may be sampling knobs for high-volume routes.
[05:38] Evan: switching gears — how do you price reserved pools? is it per-GPU per-hour or a flat monthly commitment?
[05:46] Maya: reserved capacity is typically a monthly committed amount — unit pricing per GPU-hour effectively but billed as a monthly commitment with discount tiers. we'll provide sample pricing for the sizes you asked.
[05:58] Priya: our expected steady baseline is ~40k tokens/sec across model invocations during day with spikes up to 150k for 30 minutes. how would you size that?
[06:12] Carlos: rough back-of-envelope: depends on model choice and effective throughput per GPU. if you're using an L7-ish open model, maybe X tokens/sec per A100-equivalent — we need your invocation distribution (seq length, parallelism). the benchmark will give exact numbers.
[06:30] Li: we can share a trace sample — but note we have heavy kv-cache reuse, so token/sec raw numbers may overstate cost.
[06:38] Carlos: that's helpful; kv-cache reuse reduces compute significantly. please share a representative trace.
[06:46] Priya: what's your multi-region story? we need EU data residency for some customers and NA for others — can dedicated be split?
[06:56] Maya: yes. you can provision dedicated pools per region and route traffic by policy. we also have smart routing for SLO-based routing.
[07:06] Evan: there was a note in procurement about compliance packages and longer retention of logs — any extra costs there?
[07:14] Maya: extended retention and compliance packages are add-ons; we'll include those in the pricing doc.
[07:22] Priya: curious about failover — if a reserved pool goes down, how fast is failover to standby?
[07:30] Carlos: if standby is another reserved pool in-region, failover is near-immediate at the routing layer; if you need cross-region failover we recommend asynchronous replication and a brief DNS/routing switch — typically under a minute depending on networking.
[07:46] Li: will the KV cache warm on the standby or do we lose perf?
[07:50] Carlos: cache won't be fully warm instantly. that's why warm pool pre-warming and gradual shifting are recommended, plus we can do bulk preloads for critical prefixes.
[08:04] Priya: any limitations on model variants — say we want smaller quantized model for burst and full-fp model for baseline — is that automated?
[08:14] Carlos: yes, you can configure model variants and routing policies. Redwood can automatically route to a quantized model variant when cost-sensitive or to the full model if quality checks pass. we log quality/regression metrics.
[08:28] Evan: I'm worried about complexity — multiple pools, pinned nodes, warm spares — ops burden is a concern. do you offer runbooks or managed ops?
[08:38] Maya: we have an Ops Playbook and runbooks for common patterns and also offer an optional managed operations bundle for enterprise customers.
[08:46] Priya: nice. will there be a dedicated TAM for us?
[08:49] Maya: for enterprise contracts yes, TAM is available.
[08:52] [small crosstalk] Evan: ok, planning question — we'd like to do a two-week pilot, production-representative traffic at 20% scale, test failover and burst. is that feasible?
[09:04] Carlos: absolutely. typical pilot: reserved baseline pool sized at 20% of target, a warm pool for bursts, and a test plan with synthetic traffic plus a shared trace replay. we'll instrument latency and correctness checks.
[09:18] Li: do you support replaying recorded traffic with token-level fidelity? our traces include long sequences and nested calls.
[09:26] Carlos: yes, we can replay traces and pin the sequences. note that we sometimes need to obfuscate PHI; we can work through a sanitized trace if required.
[09:38] Priya: procurement asked for a SLA figure — do you have p99 SLOs for dedicated?
[09:44] Maya: we publish SLOs for uptime; tail latency SLOs vary by model and config. for dedicated with pinned nodes we can commit to tighter latency SLOs in contract. we'll include sample SLO language.
[09:58] Evan: are there any license implications for hosting open models vs vendor models?
[10:02] Carlos: depends on the model license. Redwood maintains a model catalog with licensing notes; you'll need to check the model's redistributability for private/on-prem installs.
[10:12] Priya: competitors — we've looked at VendorX and an in-house stack; how is Redwood differentiated?
[10:18] Maya: differentiation is unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, smart routing, and production controls like tracing, rollouts, and rollout fallback logic.
[10:28] Priya: any limitations or gotchas we should plan for?
[10:31] Carlos: main ones: very large model context can increase memory pressure (plan capacity accordingly), quantization can impact edge-case outputs, and multi-region replication adds complexity. none are blockers but worth planning.
[10:46] Priya: okay, on the technical side can we get an architecture diagram for the hybrid setup (pinned nodes + warm pool + standby)?
[10:54] Maya: yes, we'll send an initial diagram and a proposed sizing.
[10:58] Evan: benchmarks — timeline? we want the pilot to start mid-november.
[11:02] Maya: we can target kickoff second week of November. I'll send a proposal and a benchmark plan this week.
[11:10] Li: during pilot we'd like visibility into token-level cost and per-request traceability for a set of routes.
[11:18] Carlos: that is standard in the console; we'll enable token-level breakdown and a debug mode for a sample of requests.
[11:26] Priya: what's the escalation path if we see regressions in output quality from quantized variants?
[11:32] Carlos: we'll set up quality monitoring tied to prompt sets and evals; if regressions exceed a threshold we'll auto-fallback to pinned baseline models and notify your team.
[11:44] Evan: last technical: networking — do you support VPC peering plus private endpoints and IP allow lists?
[11:52] Maya: yes — VPC peering, private endpoints, and IP allow lists are supported. for private installations we can provide a packaged deployable that sits within your VPC.
[12:04] Priya: ok thanks. can you also include a failure modes doc — what broken looks like for us?
[12:10] Maya: yes, we'll include a failure modes appendix.
[12:14] [pause]
[12:20] Priya: quick cost sensitivity — what's an example monthly for a small reserved cluster that meets our 20% pilot?
[12:28] Maya: i'll give a rough example in the pricing sheet; exact number depends on GPU type and discounts — we'll send a committed pricing table.
[12:36] Evan: procurement will want a term and exit terms — typical contract lengths?
[12:40] Maya: monthly, annual, and multi-year with increasing discounts. exit terms are negotiable — standard notice periods.
[12:50] Priya: one more security: we need attestation for data deletion and prove that KMS keys were revoked after decommission. is that possible?
[12:58] Carlos: yes, we can provide audit logs showing key usage and KMS events and a certificate of deletion for the data lifecycle events. we'll include details in the security pack.
[13:12] Maya: ok recap — redwood to send: 1) pilot plan and sizing diagram, 2) pricing + compliance add-ons, 3) benchmark plan and trace replay instructions, 4) failure modes and runbook.
[13:28] Priya: good. any blockers from your side?
[13:32] Maya: none; just access to a sanitized trace and decision on model variant preferences.
[13:38] Evan: scheduling — we'll aim for Nov 9 kickoff for pilot.
[13:42] Li: one small ask — can we get a pre-run checklist for infra readiness?
[13:46] Carlos: yes, we'll include a pre-run checklist with network, IAM, and sample traces.
[13:52] Priya: ok thanks.
[13:54] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and a calendar invite for the kickoff.
[14:00] [end of recording]

Carlos (SE): produce benchmark plan and trace replay instructions by 2026-10-31
